editorial.note: Little is known about the life and career of Sint Jans.

This altarpiece, which originally had two wings, is dedicated to the adoration of the newborn baby Jesus by the three magi, each of whom was represented on one of the panels. This centre panel depicts only the oldest king.

151866.title: Virgin and Child Enthroned, with Saints Jerome and John the Baptist and a Carthusian Monk
151866.creator: attributed to Jan Provoost

editorial.note: A Carthusian monk kneels in adoration before the enthroned Virgin and Child. He is presented to them by John the Baptist, while the Christ Child hands him a rosary.

151896.title: Christ Taking Leave of his Mother
151896.creator: Cornelis Engebrechtsz

editorial.note: This panel and the painting next to it formed part of a series of scenes from the life of the Virgin. Here we see Christ taking leave of his mother, in spite of her pleading with him not to go to Jerusalem.

151964.title: The Virgin and Child with Four Holy Virgins
151964.creator: Master of the Virgo inter Virgines

editorial.note: This painting is an ode to chastity. The Virgin sits in an enclosed garden, a symbol of virginity, surrounded by four other virgins (‘virgo inter virgines’).

This ‘memorial tablet’ was painted in commemoration of the four canons depicted on it. The partially decayed corpse in the open tomb reminds the viewer of his own mortality and asks for his prayers: ‘Whoever passes by, look and weep.

152033.title: The Raising of Lazarus

editorial.note: This triptych was painted to commemorate a married couple, the man and woman shown kneeling on the wings.
